# Asian Giant Softshell Turtle

The Asian giant softshell turtle, also called **Cantor’s giant softshell turtle** (*Pelochelys cantorii*), is one of the largest freshwater turtles in the world. It can grow to more than **6 feet long** and weigh over **100 pounds**. Unlike hard-shelled turtles, it has a flat, leathery shell and a long snorkel-like nose that helps it breathe while staying almost completely hidden under sand or mud. This unusual body shape makes it an excellent ambush predator.

This turtle lives in parts of **South and Southeast Asia**, including rivers, estuaries, and coastal wetlands. It spends much of its time buried in the riverbed, waiting for prey such as fish, crustaceans, and mollusks. Because it is so secretive, people rarely see it in the wild. Scientists once feared it might be nearly extinct in some regions because sightings became so uncommon.

The Asian giant softshell turtle is currently considered **critically endangered**. Its population has dropped because of **habitat destruction, water pollution, sand mining, and hunting** for meat and eggs. River development and dam construction have also damaged the sandy nesting areas females need to lay eggs. Conservation groups are now working to protect nesting sites, rescue eggs, and raise awareness about this rare species.

This turtle is important because it helps maintain balance in aquatic ecosystems by acting as both predator and scavenger. Protecting it also helps protect river habitats used by many other animals. The Asian giant softshell turtle is a reminder that even large and powerful animals can become vulnerable when their environment is threatened. Saving this species will require habitat protection, stricter laws, and continued scientific research.
